content:
Hello, I saw the the project for Planck's Law is open. I am a physics undergrad working in Quantum Computing and wanted to contribute in physlib, Is this a good project to start in ?
I have foundational knowledge required for the theoritical parts of the project, any lean specific and physlib specific things that I should keep in mind ?

Completely new to this sort of thing, so please point out any faults, any criticism is appreciated.

I also had another doubt, in Physlib/QuantumMechanics/PlanckConstant.lean @Joseph Tooby-Smith has only defined reduced planck's constant is that on purpose ? do we only want the reduced one or is it ok to define the original planck constant there itself ?

Yeah, I think we would want the original Planck's constant, and then define the reduced one from that - this would make a great first PR.

This seems like a good project to start off with. The most important thing to remember, is that small PRs are better than large ones (they end up getting into the project a lot quicker).

Understood, I will keep that in mind while I work on it.
Thank you

@Joseph Tooby-Smith As you mentioned, I have created a small pull request with just the addition of definition of Planck's Constant and lemmas regarding Real and Positive attached to it.

(https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/pull/1622)
(Think your PR link is one off, Physlib#1623, added a comment about linters, but otherwise looks good to me)

Yes, Sorry about that, I think I have fixed the linter issues now.
So for the next PR, should I cover adding a new PlancksLaw.lean file and importing it into physlib and defining SpectralRadiation ?

Also, For the different ways of defining Spectral Radiation, should I add all the definitions in terms of different variables, which would amount to approximately 14 different definitions, how should I structure them ? just name them differently ? That seems like it would be cumbersome to refer to but also useful in later cases when different forms are required ?
Reference Wikipedia:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planck's_law#Different_forms

and would you like me prove the additional Jacobian Conversion from frequency based to wavelength based as a separate lemma ?
Reference Wikipedia:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planck's_law#Correspondence_between_spectral_variable_forms

Thanks for submitting Physlib#1623. I see that you have already added h in terms of the reduced Planck constant.

For the next step, I would suggest a separate, small PR for Planck’s law rather than trying to formalize all fourteen forms at once. Start with one clearly documented canonical quantity, such as spectral radiance per unit frequency, with explicit assumptions on frequency and temperature, and then add the wavelength form through a separate conversion lemma.
To echo @Nathaneal Sajan point here, having one canonical definition and 14 lemmas relating that to the other forms is better then having 14 different definitions.

Understood, also @Joseph Tooby-Smith is there a reason we have a well defined type for temperature but not for frequency and wavelength, it feels like both would follow similar traits ? Or is that under development
I think it is just that no one has got round to doing this yet :).
Why is why it's great to have you @Samyak :)
So should I create that similar structure in Optics ?
I'll create the planck definition first tho, almost done
Yes, I think optics seems the best place for these sorts of things.

Understood, I have also created a PR containing the new definition and 2 related lemmas, and on the otherhand, I wanted to understand if you wanted to specific structure for Frequency and Wavelength, my idea was to sort of base it of Temperature with a few lemmas relating them based on Speed of Light ?

Also one doubt regarding how Dimensional Analysis works it feels like often when a quantity is defined the docstring contains the units for it but they aren't being checked by lean in the sense of how someone would do dimensional analysis to confirm that a quantity is energy, for example 1/k_B T ?
Has that concept been ignored for some reason ?

This sounds good!

We do have units in Physlib, and there's currently a bit of work trying to make them better. It is just a case that, in a lot of cases, they're actually not implemented within the quantities yet. So while we have the underlying framework, the use throughout the library hasn't been done yet. This is again just a case of this being something that we want to do, but we just haven't had the people power to do it.

https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/master/Physlib/Units/Examples.lean
@Joseph Tooby-Smith I have added a PR on the Optics Concept we discussed, I think while I had gone for Exams someone has covered the majority of the bases in Planck's Law
Added comment there. There are also some relevant PRs to this one here: Physlib#1763 and Physlib#1764

Joseph Tooby-Smith said:

Added comment there. There are also some relevant PRs to this one here: Physlib#1763 and Physlib#1764

I added this, but had to use a scaleUnit_val_pos inside the Wavelength.lean file, because of the issues with IsDimensionallyCorrect I think it can be reduced back once that is fixed to just a few lines.

I think fixing it would actually cause a conflict with PR #1763 so that's something to consider
Also I think docstrings need to be added to Units/Basic.lean no lemma has any docstring so it's kinda difficult to work with, I could do that if there aren't any conflicting PRs already working there
I think adding doc-strings to Units/Basic.lean would be good. Not aware of any conflicting PRs on that file, except for those above
@Samyak maybe you would be able to provide a review of Physlib#1721?
I'll go through it

Joseph Tooby-Smith said:

Samyak maybe you would be able to provide a review of Physlib#1721?

So I think the current structure could be changed alot, one issue right now is that there is an ongoing PR in mathlib on Lambert W function so we have to write some calculus for this until that is merged.

But the Wien's Law file should be smaller and separate and then another file just containing the math from sections B to E would be nice to have, so that later on when that PR on mathlib is merged we can fix this much more easily... (Also could be useful as generic math for other blackbody stuff)

Secondly the math is already bloated on it's own, alot of the hand rolled lemmas can just be replaced by mathlib lemmas.

Here is the list I found with a few ripgreps and LLMs, I am sure more can be reduced while refactoring it further:

• hasDerivAt_wave (lines 873–949) and hasDerivAt_freq are ~140 lines of manual HasDerivAt plumbing. Stating spectralRadianceWave_eq_profile as an equality of functions (rather than a pointwise implication) removes the two =ᶠ[𝓝 lam] congruence blocks, and deriv_const_mul/deriv_mul/deriv_div/deriv_pow/Real.deriv_exp plus fun_prop reduce each proof to ~15 lines.
• wienProfile_isMaxOn and the section-F maxima re-derive the first-derivative test via StrictMonoOn/StrictAntiOn composition. Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.DerivativeTest provides this directly: isMaxOn_Ioi_of_deriv matches the shape (deriv ≥ 0 left of the root, ≤ 0 right) → IsMaxOn (Ioi 0) root for both the profile and the physical curves.
• wienProfile_tendsto_zero_atTop (lines 800–832) re-derives xⁿ/(eˣ−1) → 0; Real.tendsto_exp_div_pow_atTop (Exp. lean:249) plus the eˣ − 1 ~ eˣ congruence gives it in a few lines. Real.tendsto_pow_mul_exp_neg_atTop_nhds_zero covers the x → 0⁺ side.

Also I could probably fix the instance issues in the documentation update itself and alongside that remove the scaleUnit_val_pos from Wavelength.lean
Hi @Samyak, maybe you could provide your comments for Physlib#1721 to the author directly on github? That would be very helpful

Nathaneal Sajan said:

Hi Samyak, maybe you could provide your comments for Physlib#1721 to the author directly on github? That would be very helpful

I could make them if that's allowed, I am free :)
I'll still post it there though
Ofcourse you are more than welcome to post reviews of PRs and engage in an iterative process with the authors.

Nathaneal Sajan said:

Ofcourse you are more than welcome to post reviews of PRs and engage in an iterative process with the authors.

The issue might be that what I am suggesting is a really big refactor, should I just create commits and push them or what's the standard procedure for this ?
I don't want to step over their work

Also as a side note, I wanted to explore writing the formalism for Pauli Groups and Clifford Operators since that's my main focus in research, I kind of have a hang of things now, who should I ask for Quantum Info related PRs ?

Thanks for asking, firstly requesting a big refactor is alright (in this case the PR is quite large so it is to be expected). The standard procedure is just putting comments on the PR and then engage in a discussion with the author. I think writing commits and pushing should only be done if you and the author agree to collaborate on the PR.
BTW a maintainer would look over your review before it is merged so you will have some oversight if that helps
Yup, got it

With regards to QuantumInfo, you can open your PR to the QuantumInfo library and maintainer for that library will review your PR. If it helps, there is a new API map format discussed in Physlib#1807, this as of now does not cover QauntumInfo, you could write one out for the API you would like to contribute and this can be reviewed before write lean. Though I am not well versed with the details of that library so please do wait for further details

@Samyak The long term aim is to integrate the QuantumInfo stuff into Physlib. So if you can put it within the framework already in Physlib this is better. Any help with this integration would be very helpful as well.

....on Lambert W function so we have to write some calculus for this until that is merged....

I have an implementation of the Lambert-W functions as part of the repository I'm working on. The principal branch code was written by a real mathematician, Pjotr Buys, who was fine if his results were to be reused (it has an Apache2.0 license). I AI-ed a negative branch based on this. If you're interested I can share this. You can always replace it later.
I was not aware of any ongoing Mathlib work... when I looked for it about a month ago, I couldn't find anything.
Mathlib #43811

I don't know about the conventions followed here for importing mathematical proofs, but from what I understand we only need the principal branch of Lambert W. But then again it could cause conflicts once the mathlib version is merged, so I guess someone needs to consider all the moving parts and recommend course of action here

Include the results need in the ./Matheamtics/ForMathlib file. With a note with what PR they relate to, and with exactly the same name as in that PR. When we bump, it will cause an error which will let us know that our versions should be removed
Majority of the stuff we need is in here Mathlib #43875
On a different note, would be nice to have a good API-map.md file for this area following the new standard

I think adding doc-strings to Units/Basic.lean would be good. Not aware of any conflicting PRs on that file, except for those above

I can do it within Physlib#1763 or we can do it later in a new PR?
